name: Check the servo command numbers and payloads
step: Check the servo command numbers and payloads
rationale:
Ported from rotorflight-lua-ethos-suite PR #2540 (issue #2444):
nothing pinned the servo command numbers, and a mapping slip there writes a
valid-looking slot on another servo with no error, so a plausible edit must not
pass unseen.

From wingflight-firmware MSP API 22.16 a servo index is the same in every servo
message (index N is servo S(N+1)), so the raw/packed index split this harness used
to pin is gone, and with it the module's raw write (124). The servo record lost its
rate: seven 16-bit fields, mid, min, max, rneg, rpos, speed, flags. The read reply
is 14 bytes and the write is 1 + 14, and the firmware refuses any other length, so
a rate left in the payload would make every servo save fail. The rate became one
setting, U16 servo_pwm_rate at the end of MSP_MIXER_CONFIG, written after the two
bus channel counts, with the old bus_servo_clone_pwm byte reserved.

The harness reads the command number and the payload off the messages the modules
build: 125 and 212 in lib/msp_servo_config.lua, 213 in lib/msp_servo_center.lua,
193 in lib/msp_servo_override.lua, the 15-byte write byte for byte, a 14-byte
reply decoded field by field, the 7-byte mixer config reply and its long and short
write forms in lib/msp_mixer_config.lua, and the PWM output count of
MSP2_WING_SERVO_TIMING in lib/msp_servo_timing.lua.
--self-test swaps one number or one field at a time in a copy of each module and
requires the pin to go red every time, after the unmodified modules have passed.
